summary: Baij Nath Puri was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Oxford from around 1950 to 1952. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1971–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1872–1873), Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1873–1876), and Government Law College, Mumbai (~1877–1879).

Bal Krishen Thapar was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at the University of the Punjab (~1941–1943). In 1981, he served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India.
Bangwei Wang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Peking University (~1983–1987), where he later became a professor around 1992.

Banikanta Kakati was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta from around 1913 to 1918. He later served as a professor at Cotton University from circa 1918 to 1949.
Barbara E. Ward, active in Sinology, studied at Newnham College (~1937–1940). She later held posts at Newnham College, the University of Cambridge, and the University of London.

Barbara Gerke is a Tibetologist who completed her D.Phil. at Oxford (~2004–2008) under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel. She held posts at Oxford, Humboldt University, the University of Vienna, and the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies.
Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She completed her studies at Queen's University (~1958–1962) and SOAS University of London (1969–1974).

Indologist Barbara Stoler Miller studied at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD ~1962–1968) under W. Norman Brown, Royal W. Weiler, and Ludo Rocher. She was Assistant Professor of Oriental Studies at Barnard College (~1968–1993).

Barbra R. Clayton is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at McGill University (~1994–2001) under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, also studying under Kameshwar Nath Mishra and G. Raj, and joined Mount Allison University (~2001).
Barend Faddegon was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Amsterdam from circa 1895 to 1906 and later held a post there from 1907 to 1944.

Barend Jan Terwiel is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Leiden University, Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1988–1992), and the University of Hamburg (~1992–2007) as Professor Dr.

Barend ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies who earned his PhD at Leiden University (~1984–1990). He held posts at the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences, Heidelberg University, and Leiden University (~2000–2013).

Barry Kerzin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Granada Hills Charter High School, the University of California, Berkeley (~1972–1976), and Keck School of Medicine of USC (~1972–1976), and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen.

Barry Sautman is a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at UCLA School of Law (~1973–1976), New York University School of Law (~1979–1981), and Columbia University (~1985–1990), and took a post at Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (~1994).
Bart Dessein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Willemen and held a post as an Associate Professor at Ghent University around 2000.

Bartholomäus Ziegenbalg was a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He served as a missionary at the Tranquebar Mission (~1706–1719) and as Probst at New Jerusalem Church, Tharangambadi (~1718–1719).

Basil Gould was a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He was educated at Winchester College (~1896–1902) and New College (~1902–1906), later serving in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1907 to 1947.

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguistics scholar who studied at Princeton (~1847–1849) and under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl at the University of Bonn (~1851–1853). He served as a professor at Johns Hopkins University from circa 1876 to 1915.

Bazar Baradiin was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and became head of the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies in 1920.
